key_findings.no_30pct_government_source_found: No government agency (FMCSA, GAO, DOT OIG, NTSB) has published a fleet-wide ELD noncompliance rate of 30% or any comparable aggregate estimate. The 30% figure traces exclusively to Joshua Kreyer (Silver Arrow Express Operating Manager) as quoted in FreightWaves — there is no independent corroboration.

cvsa_2025_roadcheck.finding: 10% of all driver out-of-service violations were for false logs/RODS falsification (332 of ~3,342 OOS drivers). HOS was top driver OOS violation at 32.4% of OOS violations. These are violation-of-OOS-drivers figures, not fleet-wide noncompliance rates.
cvsa_2025_roadcheck.note: OOS rate applies to inspected trucks presenting for roadside check — not representative of all trucks running. Roadcheck does not produce a fleet-wide ELD noncompliance prevalence rate.

cvsa_2024_roadcheck.source: CVSA International Roadcheck 2024 — via Foley.io summary
cvsa_2024_roadcheck.finding: HOS was the #1 driver violation category at 32.1% of total driver violations (870 violations). No breakdown of what share of inspected trucks had ELD violations specifically.

fmcsa_eld_revocations_2025_2026.finding: 27 ELDs revoked since January 2026; revocation pace ran 80% higher in 2025 than prior year. These are device-level revocations (manufacturer compliance), not carrier/truck noncompliance rates.

fmcsa_eld_oversight_report_april_2023.note: This is the primary government document most likely to contain fleet-wide compliance rate data. Must be retrieved via attended browser session.

freightwaves_article_source_analysis.finding: FreightWaves article relies on anecdotal expert testimony. Three industry figures quoted (Kreyer, Meiborg, Moss), none of whom cite an independent study or government dataset for the 30% figure. The article itself acknowledges the estimate is from an industry operator, not regulatory analysis.

key_findings.contradicting_signal: FMCSA broadly characterized ELD compliance as 'nearly 99% across the trucking industry' (cited in secondary sources from FMCSA materials), which directly contradicts the 30% noncompliance claim. However, the 99% claim refers to ELD adoption/registration compliance, not to ELD data integrity or log falsification — these measure different things.

suggested_revision_options.revised_claim_text: Industry observers have raised concerns about ELD log falsification and non-compliant ELD device use among a subset of carriers, though no government agency has published a fleet-wide noncompliance rate. CVSA's 2025 International Roadcheck found that 10% of all driver out-of-service violations involved false logs or records-of-duty-status falsification, and HOS violations were the top driver violation category (32.4% of OOS violations) across 56,178 inspections.
suggested_revision_options.note: Replaces unsubstantiated 30% estimate with verifiable CVSA enforcement data; frames as a known enforcement priority without fabricating a fleet-wide prevalence rate.

suggested_revision_options.revised_claim_text: [ASSUMED-N]: ~30% of trucks estimated running non-compliant ELD systems — source is single industry operator (Joshua Kreyer, Silver Arrow Express) via FreightWaves; no FMCSA, GAO, or CVSA dataset corroborates this fleet-wide rate. To validate: request FMCSA MCMIS enforcement data or obtain FMCSA ELD Oversight Report (April 2023, PDF blocked).

suggested_revision_options.rationale: The 30% figure is an unverified single-operator estimate with no regulatory corroboration and is contradicted by FMCSA's own characterization of 'nearly 99%' ELD adoption compliance. Retain only the CVSA Roadcheck HOS/false-log violation data as the factual anchor.

reasoning: The '30% non-compliant' claim traces to a single industry operator quote and cannot be independently verified through any government enforcement dataset, GAO study, or academic analysis. The CVSA Roadcheck data provides a verifiable, primary-government-adjacent source (CVSA is the enforcement body) showing that log falsification and HOS violations are significant enforcement priorities — but expressed as shares of out-of-service violations among inspected trucks, not as fleet-wide noncompliance prevalence. The widen-range option preserves a factual claim about ELD compliance enforcement while removing the unsupported '30%' figure. The FMCSA ELD Oversight Report (April 2023) remains the one potentially decisive primary source and should be retrieved via attended fetch before finalizing.
